cmad.notes: SDO is operating and NASA-funded (Living With a Star), so a CMAD is expected. The 2023 Heliophysics Senior Review report (https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/final-2023-senior-review-report-tagged.pdf) says SDO's 'draft CMADs were provided to the Senior Review panel and are nearing completion', so current SDO CMADs exist in draft. None was located publicly after searching Zenodo, the SDO/GSFC site, the HMI/JSOC and LMSAL AIA sites, the LASP EVE pages and the web (two passes). The only CMAD found is the pre-launch EVE CMAD, document EVE-T-11003 Rev. A dated 2005-01-31 (revised draft for CDR; first draft for PDR 2003-12-13), prepared by Francis G. Eparvier, EVE Project Scientist, and approved 'TNW' (Tom Woods). It is hosted as an example document in the NASA LWS GDC Program Library (https://soma.larc.nasa.gov/lws/gdc/programlibrary.html). It predates launch by five years and covers EVE only, so its front page is founding-era, instrument-level evidence, not current-team evidence. Current-team evidence came instead from the SDO Senior Review proposals (2015, 2017, 2020), the SDO team and contact pages, and the Instrument record Contacts.

instrument_coverage.notes: Reverse lookup: every record in the SMWG clone (hpde/SMWG @ b8c8b803) was searched for ObservatoryID spase://SMWG/Observatory/SDO. Only AIA, EVE and HMI match, and the registry listing https://spase-metadata.org/SMWG/Instrument/SDO/ shows the same three. The SDO instruments page, the Definitive Publications page, the 2020 Senior Review fact sheet and the record's own Description all give the same three-instrument payload, so the SPASE coverage is complete. EVE's MEGS and ESP are subsystems within EVE (EVE record Description), not separate instruments.

notes: Operating span: the SDO Observatory record has no OperatingSpan element. Start is the launch date given in the record's Description (11 Feb 2010); the Senior Review proposals give the prime-mission start as 2010-05-01. Stop is null because SDO is still operating (continued by the 2023 Senior Review). Curators may wish to add an OperatingSpan to the record.

Mission overview paper selection is confident: (Pesnell et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9841-3) names SDO in its title, appeared in the Solar Physics SDO issue within two years of launch, has 3245 Crossref citations, is listed as the 'Mission Paper' on the SDO Definitive Publications page, and was the top Semantic Scholar hit. SciX was not queried directly (no API token); the SDO site links a SciX public library of SDO publications. Only three authors, above the 1–2-author science-result threshold. Backward scan: not alphabetized (Pesnell, Thompson, Chamberlin), so all three are Strong. There are no 4th or 5th authors.

AIA author list (n=47): a literal backward scan finds only a 4-name sorted tail (Beardsley, Clapp, Lang, Waltham) because the list is alphabetized in institutional blocks: LMSAL at positions 3–26 (one inversion, Wuelser before Wolfson), SAO at 27–34, Stanford at 35–36, then the remaining partners. Treated as partially alphabetized with prefix = Lemen, Title (2 authors), following the skill's worked example for this paper and the rule to err against awarding position evidence. Akin (position 3) is not promoted. Selection is confident: the paper is linked from the AIA Instrument record, listed on the SDO Definitive Publications page, and has 4346 Crossref citations.

EVE author list (n=18): the backward scan finds a sorted tail of exactly five (Bailey, Fuller-Rowell, Sojka, Tobiska, Viereck), so the list is partially alphabetized with a 13-author prefix. Prefix positions 1–3 (Woods, Eparvier, Hock) are the same as a non-alphabetized reading would give. Selection is confident: SDO Definitive Publications page, Semantic Scholar agreement, published within the time window (online Jan 2010, print 2012).

HMI has two companion description papers in the same issue: (Schou et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9842-2), the instrument design and calibration paper listed as the HMI paper on the SDO Definitive Publications page, and (Scherrer et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9834-2), the investigation overview. Neither is alphabetized (sorted tail of 3 in each). Both have the same three people in positions 1–3 (Schou, Scherrer, Bush), so the choice does not change the leads and the selection is treated as confident; both are linked in information_urls. Author lists were confirmed against the NTRS copies of both papers, which also gave the Stanford and LMSAL affiliations.

Observatory-run scoping: each instrument contributes its leads only (paper positions 1–3 plus every qualifying-role person in its Instrument record Contacts). Authors at positions 4–5 of each instrument paper, Akin (AIA position 3, alphabetized part), and depth co-authors with another signal (SMWG Person record, or several SDO papers) are listed individually as excluded. The remaining instrument-paper co-authors and the members of instrument-level team lists (HMI Science Team page, 42 entries, last modified 2011-11-15; EVE personnel page) are instrument-team depth. They are not listed individually and belong to the AIA, EVE and HMI Instrument-record runs.

SDO Senior Review proposals (2015, 2017, 2020, hosted at http://hmi.stanford.edu/papers/) are treated as mission-level authored documents (Medium). Their author lines are Pesnell, Scherrer, Schrijver, Woods (2015) and Pesnell, Scherrer, Cheung, Woods (2017, 2020). This gives observatory scope to Scherrer, Woods, Cheung and Schrijver. Reviewer: if observatory scope should be limited to the overview paper and CMADs, these four revert to instrument scope; their confidence and roles do not change.

SDO and instrument web pages that name an instrument PI were used to corroborate the Instrument record Contacts. They did not lift a Contacts-only PI to Strong on this Observatory run, so Cheung, Schrijver and Meng Jin are Medium. Scherrer, Woods and Title are Strong through their paper positions.

Role mapping: 'EVE Project Scientist' (Eparvier) is recorded as InstrumentScientist, the instrument-level role, so it is not read as SDO's Project Scientist on the Observatory record; the exact title is stated in role_evidence. 'SDO Deputy Project Scientist' (Thompson, Chamberlin) has no legal SPASE role, so both carry Author only; the title is recorded in their evidence. Bush's HMI 'Program Manager' title is a non-qualifying role and is context only.

Stale provider pages: the SDO instruments page still lists Alan Title as AIA PI, and the SDO team page (archived 2025-06-16) lists Mark Cheung. The AIA Instrument record (Meng Jin PI; Cheung, Schrijver and Title as FormerPI) is up to date and agrees with Jin's LMSAL homepage (PI since 2022). The current SDO site footer names Michael Kirk as NASA Official; in June 2025 it named Barbara Thompson. The live SDO team and contact pages return HTTP 403, so the Wayback Machine copies from 2025-06-16 were used.

Person-record issues for the reviewer: (1) Rock I. Bush is linked to spase://SMWG/Person/R.Bush (same person, per an earlier curator ruling). That record's affiliation (University of California, Berkeley) conflicts with Stanford on both HMI papers. (2) The Mark.C.M.Cheung record gives Stanford University; the SDO team page gives Lockheed Martin for his AIA PI period. (3) Theodore D. Tarbell has two Person records (Ted.D.Tarbell and Theodore.D.Tarbell). (4) The Alan.M.Title and James.R.Lemen records use the old laboratory name 'Lockheed Palo Alto Research Laboratory'. (5) Karel.Schrijver is Carolus J. Schrijver on paper bylines. (6) Rick.Bogart is presumed to be Richard S. Bogart (excluded here). (7) No Person records exist for Phillip C. Chamberlin, Francis G. Eparvier, Rachel A. Hock or Jesper Schou.

Rachel A. Hock: the EVE paper byline is 'R. Hock'. The full name comes from her first-author EVE MEGS calibration paper with Chamberlin and Woods (Hock et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-010-9520-9) and the 2007 SPIE EVE MEGS paper (Chamberlin et al. 2007, 10.1117/12.734116). Verify identity downstream.

Barbara J. Thompson: Wikipedia says she was SDO project scientist 'through development and early flight', but the SDO team page has Pesnell accepting that post in 2005 (pre-launch). ProjectScientist is not attached; a reviewer with SDO project history could confirm.

Phillip C. Chamberlin affiliation: NASA Goddard at the time of the overview paper and his Deputy Project Scientist role (NASA Science profile). The EVE personnel page now groups him under University of Colorado / LASP. Era-match downstream.
Record Contacts list only Pesnell (ProjectScientist). The RevisionHistory note initials 'JWL' belong to a metadata editor; they were not resolved to a person and are not authorship evidence.

Semantic Scholar rate-limited most queries (no API key). The one successful search returned all five SDO-issue papers (overview, AIA, both HMI papers, EVE) with author counts matching Crossref, and a later per-paper lookup confirmed the EVE byline. Crossref has no affiliations or ORCIDs for these Solar Physics 275 papers. The ORCIDs given come from SMWG Person records (Cheung, Jin) and Crossref (Aschwanden, excluded).

Calibration and component papers were not used for candidates on this Observatory run: AIA initial calibration (Boerner et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-011-9804-8) and EVE MEGS (Hock et al. 2012, 10.1007/s11207-010-9520-9). The HMI vector-field pipeline paper (Hoeksema et al. 2014, 10.1007/s11207-014-0516-8) is a data-product paper; it is linked in information_urls, but its authors belong to the HMI vector-field data records' runs.

information_urls omits links already present verbatim in the target records: the SDO web page and HelioData (Observatory record), and the AIA, EVE and HMI provider home pages (Instrument records). Description papers are listed even where an Instrument record already links them; the AIA paper is already in the AIA record, so the writer should skip duplicates by URL.
